title: Dynamic Eval Gates with Weighted Prompt Coverage for Canary and Shadow Traffic
creator: Elliot Zhang
description:
Problem: Current canary and shadow rollouts rely on monolithic score thresholds which cause noisy alerts for low-frequency behavioural regressions and lack signal prioritization across prompt types. Goal: Build a dynamic gating layer that evaluates canary and shadow traffic against a weighted inventory of prompts (prompt coverage) and behavioral anchors, producing multi-level gates (informational, advisory, critical) and a probability-based auto-rollback suggestion. The system should operate on per-customer and global scopes, support gradual enforcement (soft -> hard gates), and expose clear reasons and example traces to the Console for operators.

Approach:
- Construct a lightweight prompt coverage catalog (indexed by intent cluster, token-length bucket, and risk label). Each prompt entry carries a weight based on production frequency and business impact.
- For each rollout bucket (canary, A/B, shadow), compute sampled eval metrics aggregated by weighted coverage and by behavioral signatures (toxicity, hallucination markers, instruction-following fidelity).
- Define gate rules that combine delta thresholds (relative quality drop) and absolute failure rates; map rule violations to severity tiers.
- Implement a streaming monitor that computes rolling-window deltas and surfaces the top contributing prompts and example responses.
- Integrate with rollback orchestrator to propose (not auto-execute) rollback when a critical gate fires, with an option for customer-configured auto-execute.

Trade-offs considered:
- Weighting prompts by production frequency improves signal-to-noise but biases toward common cases; to mitigate, include a risk multiplier for low-frequency, high-impact prompts.
- Streaming window size affects sensitivity vs volatility; default to 30m rolling with tunable parameters per project.
- Full proof-of-eval for every request is costly; we will use sampled shadow traffic with stratified sampling keyed by customer, endpoint, and prompt cluster.

Acceptance criteria:
- Console shows gate status (OK/Advisory/Critical) per rollout within 2s of metric window end.
- Top-10 contributing prompts and 5 example traces for each fired gate are linkable from the gate view.
- Gate decision logic operates on weighted coverage and produces consistent advisories in a synthetic test harness (see test plan).
- Rollback proposal messages populate the existing rollback queue with actionable metadata (triggering prompt IDs, delta metrics, affected customers).
acceptance_criteria: Gate status visible in Console for each rollout within 2s of window end
Top contributors and example traces accessible from gate detail
Weighted-coverage delta rules evaluated in the synthetic test harness and pass against baseline model
Rollback proposals include sufficient context for on-call to act
Sampling maintains <10% CPU overhead on runtime observability pipeline
implementation_notes:
Plan: 1) Build prompt coverage catalog schema and importer (CSV + Confluence mapping). 2) Implement weighted aggregator in observability service as sidecar stream job. 3) Add gate rule engine with tunable bindings and severity mapping. 4) Console integration for gate visualization and trace drilldown. 5) Hook into existing rollback orchestration with a non-destructive proposal workflow.

MVP scope: global scope + per-customer advisory gates; no auto-execute. Later: per-customer hard gates and auto-execute opt-in.

Metrics to monitor: false-positive advisory rate, time-to-detect, rollback proposal accuracy, CPU/RAM overhead of aggregator.
comments: 2025-01-11 — Maya Perez: Spiked a strawman rule set (relative drop >5% AND abs fail rate >0.5%) in the staging harness; produced a few false positives on low-volume intents. Need to add risk multiplier for low-frequency prompts.
2025-01-13 — Data Eng (review): Recommended using stratified sampling by customer ID + endpoint to avoid spike bias. Also suggested using reservoir sampling for long-tail prompt coverage tracking.

2025-01-15 — SRE (review): Concern about adding another streaming job; suggested implementing aggregator as an extension to existing observability sidecar to share memory pools. Will prototype with canary workload next week.

2025-01-17 — Product (review): PM asks for clearer CSV/Confluence mapping spec for prompt weights; requested an initial default weighting algorithm (freq * impact_score) and UI to override per-project.

2025-01-20 — Engineering update: Prototype of weighted aggregator completed; bench shows ~6% CPU increase on staging observability cluster for 10k rps of sampled traffic. Working on gate rule DSL and Console mockups.

2025-01-21 — Design feedback (K. Rivera): Gate UI should highlight severity timeline and allow 'why' drilldown to show contributing prompts with mini-diffs between models. Will provide mock assets by 2025-01-24.
test_plan: Run synthetic regression harness that injects controlled quality drops across 20 prompt clusters; verify gate severity matches expected mapping
Create per-customer shadow runs with stratified sampling; assert rollback proposals include correct customer bucket metadata
Load test aggregator at 50k rps sampling to validate CPU/RAM scaling
Manual runbook drill: on Critical gate fire, follow proposal -> rollback queue -> canary revert sequence and validate metrics return to baseline
